subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should workspace scans treat an ignore file over 4 MiB as a terminal exclusion of that directory subtree, accepting that existing oversized ignore files hide otherwise discoverable content?
rationale: The cap mitigates unbounded memory consumption, but the chosen fallback changes user-visible scan results for existing workspaces and cannot be resolved from tests alone.

options.title: Approve the terminal exclusion policy
options.body: Accept the 4 MiB fail-closed behavior after refreshed current-head proof demonstrates normal, oversized, negated, and symlinked cases.

options.title: Choose a compatibility-preserving fallback
options.body: Keep the bounded read but direct a different oversized-file behavior if silently hiding a subtree is not acceptable for existing workspaces.

recommendation.title: Approve the terminal exclusion policy
recommendation.body: Accept the 4 MiB fail-closed behavior after refreshed current-head proof demonstrates normal, oversized, negated, and symlinked cases.
